account: Today has been largely routine: office business, a market walk, tea with my neighbour, and the builder's afternoon review. My neighbour reported no problems around the cottages and mentioned freight asking about deliveries at the bakery; I also heard freight offering ferry crossings. I have no evidence that these ordinary activities signify anything unusual. The builder reported no confirmed defects at the bridge, landing, or warehouse. After some missed communication, I offered two emeralds total for a preventive inspection of the town hall doors, bridge decking, and landing, payable upon written findings, with no repairs or extra charges authorized. The secretary has now come to my home after dark to report that the builder accepted those terms and tomorrow's 16:30 appointment. The remaining questions are which landing to inspect and his request for a writable book; the secretary has not authorized additional spending. This late visit appears to be a practical effort to clarify the inspection instructions, not evidence of an emergency. I have not yet specified which landing or answered the book request.
